definition: A distributed training approach that splits a single model's layers or parameters across multiple devices, since the model is too large to fit on one device.
details: Model parallelism is essential for training today's largest LLMs, whose parameter counts far exceed the memory capacity of any single GPU.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Think of it this way: A distributed training approach that splits a single model's layers or parameters across multiple devices, since the model is too large to fit on one device. And here is the clever part: Model parallelism is essential for training today's largest LLMs, whose parameter counts far exceed the memory capacity of any single GPU. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Model Parallelism — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
